TWO GAPS, both flagged on the rows. The pulp mill investment cost is quoted in 'USD' with NO base year anywhere in the brief; the underlying study is EBRD & POYRY 2012 so 2012_USD is the likely basis, but it is not stated and has not been assumed, which means those rows will not be converted. Table 3's cost functions are in MEUR, also with no year.

Table 4's first three columns each hold TWO products: the bare number is the dried pulp and the bracketed one the slush. Since 2026-09-25 each such column is ONE example with two cases, [dried] and [slush], at the start of each row's note (rule: cases within one table are one example); the gap reaches 40% (17.2 against 12.0 GJ/t for bleached kraft), so the cases must not be averaged. Column positions are unambiguous in this table - unlike I02 and I03 - but the arithmetic is not: see below.

Table 4's sub-rows reconcile with their block totals in every column but two. Recycled paper's 'For steam generation' cell reads 0.6 where its own sub-rows and the 'Fuel use' total both give 0.4. Kraft paperboard's 'Total energy use' reads 7.6 where its stated definition (fuel use + external electricity) gives 8.2; 7.6 is what using the backpressure figure instead of external electricity would give. Several other columns are out by 0.1, which is rounding. All recorded as printed.
Table 4's footnote cites Wiberg 2012, whose title dates the survey to 2011, while the Figure 5 caption on p.5 dates the same dataset to 2007. The brief does not resolve it.

Table 3 is taken wholesale from Jonsson et al. 2013 and Table 4's energy block from Wiberg 2012. Under design doc D7 those are the sources and the brief is the via, but neither is held or registered, so source-id is the brief for now and the originals are listed in _cited-sources.csv for a registration pass - the same two-level attribution UKERC and IPCC got.

Changes against the repo copy: (1) The dried and slush products of Table 4's three two-product columns were six technologies; each column is now ONE example (rule: cases within one table are one example): digester_bleached, digester_unbleached, pulper_tmp, with '[dried]' / '[slush]' at the start of each row's note, one description and one state-of-development per column, and the route-level capacity and capex rows marked '[both cases - route level]'. Process labels unchanged. (2) The 18 fuel flow rows (oil = the three 'External, oil/other' rows; biomass-solid = the three 'Internal' rows) stay as DERIVED per-case totals with their sum formulas (allowed: sums of printed values); the 54 printed component rows, one per Table 4 cell, are in the new _fuel-components.csv sidecar (not loaded). New vocabulary terms needed: variant 'bleached', 'unbleached', 'tmp'.
